subject: Post-call: Redwood + Acme integration recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-call: Redwood + Acme integration recap & next steps

Hi Jordan and Sara —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call so we have alignment and clear next steps. TL;DR: Acme needs low-latency streaming chat, reliable structured outputs for downstream processing, and a reranking/embeddings flow for search relevance. Redwood can cover these via streaming responses, function calling + structured outputs, and our embeddings + reranking pipeline.

Pain points you shared:
- Current chat stack has inconsistent latency (~600-900ms) and stalls under load.
- Generations are sometimes missing the structured fields your downstream services expect, causing failed ingest.
- Embeddings quality and reranking speed are limiting search relevance and freshness.

Goals we discussed:
- Sub-300ms interactive latency for 95th percentile on typical sessions.
- Deterministic structured output (schema-first) for downstream ingestion.
- Relevance improvement via fast embedding + rerank path for top-K.

Integration / product fit notes:
- SDK changes: upgrade client to Redwood SDK v1.3 (adds streaming handler hooks + function-calling helpers). We can share a short diff and sample handler for your node/python services.
- Function calling: define a consistent JSON schema for the actions your app uses; Redwood will enforce schema validation and return structured payloads you can consume directly.
- Streaming: support for chunked token streaming to render quicker responses in the UI; works with our KV cache to keep cost down.
- Embeddings & reranking: we recommend using Redwood embeddings for recall and our lightweight reranker for top-K reordering; batching + prefix caching will keep token cost low.

Attachments: integration_mvp_plan.pdf (high level timeline, MVP scope, and milestones).

Proposed next steps:
1) Schedule a 60-min SE deep-dive (architecture + SDK pairing) — Vivek/Dev to run.
2) Share your security questionnaire and any SSO/KMS requirements (Sara to share).
3) Redwood to provide a short SDK diff + sample function-calling payload by EOD Friday.

Can you confirm availability for the SE call next week? I can do Tue/Wed mornings PST.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

marissa@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0134

Hi Jordan —

Quick technical responses to the points you raised:

1) Schema enforcement: Redwood supports schema-first function calling. You define the JSON schema for each function/action; the runtime validates and will return an explicit validation error if output doesn't match. We also provide optional pre-hooks if you want to run company-specific validators.

2) Embeddings & reranking scale: for a ~5M doc corpus we typically recommend sharded batching with incremental refresh. Typical P95 latency for an embedding + top-100 rerank call is in the 120-250ms range with dedicated capacity; on shared hosted capacity plan for ~250-450ms. We'll share benchmarking notes tailored to your average doc size.

3) SDK changes: example summary below — I'll attach a short snippet. High-level: SDK v1.3 adds: streaming callbacks (on_chunk/on_complete), function-calling helpers (schema registration + typed responses), and a small rerank helper that takes candidate embeddings and returns reorder scores. Migration is usually a few hours for a single service.

Sample function-calling payload (snippet):
{
  "function": "create_invoice",
  "args": { "customer_id": "1234", "amount": 199.99, "currency": "USD" }
}

I'll add the sdk_changes_snippet.txt and a small schema_examples.json to the repo for your engineers. For the SE deep-dive I suggest we pair on a small `chat + function-calling` demo using one of your endpoints and walk through streaming UI integration.

Proposed SE call time: Tue 11 Feb 09:00 PST (Marissa to confirm calendar invite).
